text.p: The central bank heavily funded banks on Thursday as cash demand picked up ahead of Friday's hefty salary payments in the public sector, bankers said.

It lent banks 34.8 trillion lira overnight money at 75 percent, up from the 27.8 trillion it funded on Wednesday. Overnight money also traded at 74.75 in the morning before a cash squeeze intensified.
Banks repaid the central bank a total of 40 trillion lira in overnight borrowings from Wednesday and repo deals from a previous open market auction.

The lira closed easier at 98,525 to the dollar on banks' dollar demand, despite tight liquidity and minor but persistent central bank intervention. It opened at 98,560 against Wednesday's 98,410 close.
Bankers said dollar demand was relatively firm and the central bank tried to restrain the U.S. currency at around 98,500 by selling dollars for lira all day.
Yields on t-bills and bonds with 1997 maturities ended firmer by around one point on cash shortage ahead of Friday's public sector salary payments.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper rose to 119.34 from Wednesday's 117.53 percent. The second most active October 30, 1997 paper yielded 118.18 percent, up from 117.20 percent average.
